tips.title: Colourful vegetables
tips.body: Aim to fill about half your plate with vegetables of different colours.

tips.title: Whole grains
tips.body: Brown rice, oats, ragi, millets and whole wheat roti keep you fuller for longer.

tips.title: Dals and pulses
tips.body: Dal, rajma, chana and sprouts give protein and fibre at a low cost.

tips.title: Whole fruit
tips.body: A piece of fruit makes an easy snack that comes with fibre.

tips.title: Eggs, fish and lean chicken
tips.body: These are convenient protein sources that fit many meals.

tips.title: Paneer, curd and milk
tips.body: Dairy adds protein and calcium. Choose plain curd over sweetened versions.

tips.title: Tofu, soy and legumes
tips.body: Soy chunks, tofu, lentils and chickpeas are great plant-based protein sources.

tips.title: Nuts and seeds
tips.body: A small handful of nuts or seeds adds healthy fats and extra energy.

tips.title: Extra healthy calories
tips.body: Add a banana with peanut butter or a glass of milk or soy milk between meals to build up calories gently.

tips.title: Fibre-rich foods
tips.body: Salads, sprouts and vegetables can help you feel satisfied on fewer calories.

tips.title: Sugary drinks
tips.body: Cold drinks, packaged juices and sweet chai add calories without keeping you full.

tips.title: Deep-fried snacks
tips.body: Samosa, pakora and chips are fine now and then. Try baking or air-frying for everyday snacking.

tips.title: Sweets and desserts
tips.body: Enjoy mithai and desserts in small portions on special occasions.

tips.title: Refined flour (maida)
tips.body: Swap maida breads and noodles for whole wheat versions when you can.

tips.title: Packaged salty snacks
tips.body: Chips, namkeen and instant noodles are easy to overeat. Check labels for salt and fat.

tips.title: Processed meats
tips.body: Sausages, salami and similar items are best kept occasional.

tips.title: Very large portions of white rice
tips.body: Balance rice with dal and vegetables so the plate has more variety.

tips.title: Skipping meals to save calories
tips.body: Very long gaps can lead to overeating later. Regular, smaller meals often feel easier.

tips.title: Too much salt
tips.body: Go easy on pickles, papad and salty snacks, and taste your food before adding more salt.

tips.title: Refined sugar and sweet drinks
tips.body: Choose unsweetened drinks and keep sweets small. Ask your doctor or a dietitian what is right for you.

tips.title: Pair carbs with protein and fibre
tips.body: Having dal, curd or vegetables with your roti or rice makes meals more balanced.

tips.title: Gentler cooking methods
tips.body: Steaming, grilling and pressure cooking use less oil than frying.

tips.title: Eat slowly
tips.body: Taking 15 to 20 minutes over a meal helps you notice when you are full.

tips.title: Plan your meals
tips.body: A simple plan for the week makes healthy choices easier on busy days.

tips.title: Protein at every meal
tips.body: Including some protein in each meal can help you stay full between meals.

tips.title: No food is "bad"
tips.body: Balance matters more than perfection. One treat does not undo your progress.

tips.title: Try a smaller plate
tips.body: A slightly smaller plate can make comfortable portions feel more satisfying.

tips.title: Add a snack
tips.body: A healthy snack between meals can make it easier to reach your energy needs.

tips.title: Sip water through the day
tips.body: Small, regular sips are easier than drinking a lot at once.

tips.title: Keep a bottle handy
tips.body: A water bottle on your desk or bag is a simple reminder to drink.

tips.title: Lighter drink choices
tips.body: Plain water, nimbu pani without much sugar, or unsweetened buttermilk are good everyday options.

tips.title: A lighter dinner
tips.body: Try to finish a balanced dinner two to three hours before bed.

tips.title: A small, simple snack if hungry
tips.body: A banana or a small bowl of curd can be enough if you feel hungry near bedtime.

tips.title: A few almonds or walnuts
tips.body: A small handful can be a satisfying evening snack.

tips.title: Caffeine-free warm drinks
tips.body: Warm milk, plant milk or a caffeine-free herbal tea can be part of a calm wind-down.

tips.title: Caffeine late in the day
tips.body: Tea, coffee, cola and energy drinks can make it harder to fall asleep.

tips.title: Heavy, oily or very spicy meals
tips.body: Large or rich meals close to bedtime can leave you uncomfortable.

tips.title: Lots of fluids right before bed
tips.body: Drink enough earlier in the day so you are not up at night.

tips.title: Sugary snacks at night
tips.body: Sweets close to bedtime can leave you feeling restless.
